title: Garry Tan's unconventional founder advice: be a super-knife, stay small, get therapy early
summary: Garry Tan, at Stanford ETL, shares lessons from his own mistakes (including turning down Palantir) and 20 years in startups and YC. He argues founders should be multi-skilled generalists, act small and hands-on with early users, deal with childhood baggage early, and work on weird problems they uniquely understand.

principles.text: Don't box yourself into one narrow role; be a generalist who can do many things.
principles.quote: you are not a tiny washer in a machine you should be everything you should not Define yourself just because the machine wants you to be an interchangeable part in the machine

principles.text: Act small even when small: do unscalable things and talk to users directly as the CEO.
principles.quote: the whole Advantage is that you're a real human being we are so starved for real authentic connection that if you can just go talk to people and say hey I'm the CEO what do you need like that is the most powerful thing

principles.text: Reply to every customer email within minutes and fix bugs on the spot.
principles.quote: we would aim to reply to every single email within 10 minutes of receiving it and if there was a bug we'd fix it on the spot

principles.text: A single human reply lifts return rates; even devtools are effectively consumer go-to-market.
principles.quote: if someone posted and did not get a reply only 16% of people would come back to that Forum but if you got even one reply 26 person percent would come back

principles.text: Startups run on a loop of co-founders, product, customers and capital; when one stalls, push another and come back.
principles.quote: if you can't get any more of any one of these things go to some of something else go get that and then come back to those other things

principles.text: Ignore media hype and pick weird problems you uniquely know; the best ideas often seem like bad ones.
principles.quote: ignore all of that and then focus on you know what do I uniquely know and what do I believe in and even if it's really weird maybe I should pull on that thread
